message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported revenue of 1.85 billion dollars for the third fiscal quarter ended 2026-07-31, up 36.54 percent from 1.35 billion dollars a year earlier [D1]. Orders were 2.09 billion dollars, up 56 percent, in the second consecutive quarter with orders above 2 billion dollars [D1]. Net income was 397 million dollars and non-GAAP earnings per share were 3.07 dollars, against non-GAAP earnings per share of 1.72 dollars a year earlier [D1]. Cash flow from operations was 437 million dollars and free cash flow was 403 million dollars, compared with 322 million dollars and 291 million dollars in the prior-year quarter [D1]. Gross margin was 69 percent and operating margin was 33.2 percent, up 820 basis points year over year and above the long-term target range of 31 percent to 32 percent [D3].

The Communications Solutions Group reported revenue of 1.35 billion dollars, up 43 percent, reflecting 56 percent growth in commercial communications and 14 percent growth in aerospace, defense and government [D1]. The Electronic Industrial Solutions Group reported revenue of 501 million dollars, up 21 percent, with growth across the semiconductor, general electronics and automotive and energy markets [D1]. Commercial communications delivered its first 1 billion dollar quarter at 1.006 billion dollars, and wireline revenue exceeded wireless revenue for the first time [D3]. Software and services both grew double digits and represented approximately 33 percent of revenue, while annual recurring revenue was 24 percent of the mix [D3]. Management tied the orders to the rapid scaling of the AI infrastructure ecosystem and to rising test intensity as design margins shrink, which requires testing at the signal, bit and protocol levels [D4].

Fourth fiscal quarter guidance is revenue of 1.93 billion dollars to 1.95 billion dollars, a mid-point representing growth of approximately 37 percent, and non-GAAP earnings per share of 3.34 dollars to 3.40 dollars on approximately 172 million diluted shares [D1]. Analysts had expected revenue of 1.82 billion dollars and earnings per share of approximately 2.68 dollars for that quarter [D2]. Management said supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue and that demand is not the limiter, with conversion expected to be nonlinear for several quarters [D3]. The chief financial officer said the one-time tariff impacts this year artificially raised fiscal 2026 profitability and will not repeat [D3]. Acquisition integration is largely complete one quarter ahead of schedule, and management expects 80 percent to 90 percent of the 100 million dollar cost synergy target on a run rate basis exiting the fiscal year [D3].

Shares climbed 2.6 percent in pre-market trading after the results, with the wireline business benefiting substantially from accelerating AI data centre investment [D2]. The mean of 12 short-term price targets is 418.42 dollars, indicating a potential upside of 30 percent, with a standard deviation of 19.48 dollars, a lowest estimate of 390.00 dollars and a most optimistic estimate of 452.00 dollars [D5]. The consensus estimate for the current year rose 11 percent over the last 30 days, with three estimates moving higher and no negative revision [D5]. The same write-up states that price targets mislead investors far more often than they guide and that business incentives often result in inflated targets [D5]. Analysts pressed on whether demand is sustainable and whether supply constraints are limiting the guidance, a tone the summary described as pressing [D3]. Management described its funnel as an all-time high, guided fourth quarter orders slightly above the third quarter's level and put the 6G opportunity above the 5G cycle [D4].
